# 20 Close two ways past the URL allowlist and the style rejection list

## Outcome

The two sinks ticket 13 was written to guard actually hold: a scheme-relative URL cannot smuggle
itself past the check by hiding a control character inside, and a `url(` cannot smuggle itself past
by spelling itself with a CSS escape.

## Why this ticket exists

Round 4's review found both, and the orchestrator reproduced both against the built pipeline:

- `click A href "/<TAB>/evil.example"` — **admitted, zero diagnostics.** `rejectUrl` strips control
  characters from the front of the string and from the scheme candidate, but runs its
  scheme-relative `^[/\\][/\\]` test on the *unstripped* text. Browsers strip ASCII tab out of a
  URL before resolving it, so what the author gets is `//evil.example`: navigation to another
  origin, which is exactly what ticket 13's criterion says must be dropped.
- `style A background-image:\75 rl(https://e.example/b)` — **admitted, zero diagnostics.** The
  rejection list matches the literal text `url(`. CSS resolves `\75 ` to `u` inside an ident, so
  this is `url(` by the time it reaches a browser. Two further spellings are admitted the same way:
  `u\72 l(...)`, and the same escape behind a custom property (`--x:\75 rl(...)`).

Ticket 13 got the hard part right — `URL(`, `url (`, `image-set(url(…))`, uppercase and
tab-bearing `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `//` and `/\` are all correctly refused. These
are the two seams left open, and both defeat the guarantee rather than dent it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every scheme-relative form is refused with a diagnostic, whatever control characters or
  spaces are hidden inside it: `//evil.example`, `/\evil.example`, `/<TAB>/evil.example`,
  `/<NUL>\evil.example`, `<SPACE>//evil.example`. Run the check on the fully-stripped string, not
  on the raw one.
- [ ] A style value spelling a rejected function with a CSS escape is refused:
  `\75 rl(...)`, `u\72 l(...)`, `\65 xpression(...)`, and the same behind a custom property name.
  Decide how: resolving CSS escapes before matching, or refusing a `\` in a value outright — the
  second is cruder and cheaper, and no value this board needs contains a backslash. Whichever you
  pick, say why in the code.
- [ ] Everything ticket 13 already refuses stays refused, and everything it already admits stays
  admitted — its 47 tests pass unmodified. In particular `rgb(255, 0, 0)` and
  `color-mix(in srgb, rgb(1,2,3), #fff)` must still be accepted; ticket 19 exists because a
  legitimate paren-bearing value was being destroyed.
- [ ] Each bypass gets a test named for what it defeats, not for its mechanism, so a future reader
  sees the property being protected.

## Test seam

`buildClassModel(document: ClassDocument): ClassModelResult` — unit level, hand-built fixtures,
extending the existing test file. This is the board's security boundary: a silently-passing
allowlist is worse than none.
